question: The current in the bulb will stop flowing:

options.text: when the switch is turned on

solution:
The correct answer is __**if the circuit is broken**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electric Current**__

 __
 
• A **stream of charged particles, such as electrons (negative charge) or ions, travelling through an electrical conductor or a vacuum** is known as an electric current. 
 
• **Charge carriers are the moving particles** that, depending on the conductor, can be of different types of particles.
 
• In** motors, generators, inductors, and transformers, magnetic fields **produced by electric currents are employed. 
 
• Electric current travels from a **cell's positive electrode to its negative electrode, or from a cell's high potential to its low potential**.
 
• Only when a **circuit is complete or in a form of a closed loop, the flow of current is seen**.
 
• The** flow of current in a bulb or any conductor** will stop if **there is any breakage in the circuit**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Positive and negative terminals **are regarded as having** high and low potential**, respectively.
 
• Although** negative charge always moves from low potential to high potential**, **positive charge always moves from high potential to low potential**. 
 
• So, we can say that the **direction of current is always opposite to the direction of flow of electron **is low potential to high potential.
 
• A **power source, like a battery**, is required for a circuit, and** current must flow through a conductor, like a wire**.
 
• Components like** bulbs, buzzers, and motors** convert **power into light**, sound, and motion.
